Details: FormVariable["q"] or FormVariable["tau"] is the inert independent variable of a parsed modular-form definition.
ModularFormDefinition replaces the declared variable symbol by this atom before anything is evaluated, so a later assignment to the symbol never changes a definition.

FormParameter[id] is an inert relative-normalization unknown of a definition. Its ID is the definition family's ID followed by the declared spelling, so the joint F and G recipes of one family share their unknowns.
Unknowns are resolved by ModularFormGetCoeff or SolveModularCoefficients; they are never Stage 5 model parameters.

ModularFormDefinition[{f1, ...}, var, opts] parses a modular-form definition held: the components (a literal list, or a symbol whose stored value is the list) may use var, numeric constants, declared NormalizationParameters and the scalar ingredients ScalarModularExpression and HypergeometricK.
ModularFormDefinition[qexp] defines a form by an explicitly finite QExpansionData (a literal value or a symbol bound to it); a jet defines only its known coefficients.

Undeclared symbols fail with UndeclaredSymbol; executable or unsupported heads, symbols with DownValues and non-lists fail with InvalidDefinition. Options: Coordinate, NormalizationParameters, FamilyID.

QExpansionData[data] is an immutable vector q-series: per component an exponent -> coefficient map with exact rational exponents, the component cutoffs (every exponent below a cutoff is known; the remainder is O(q^cutoff)), the common cutoff, arithmetic, precision, coefficient binding and source.
qexp["Cutoff"], qexp["Binding"] and qexp["Components"] read fields. An empty truncation is never evidence of the zero function.
QExpansionExpression[qexp, z] gives the components of QExpansionData as finite sums in z with their remainders O[z]^cutoff; rational and negative exponents are kept and the remainder is never erased.
z must be a symbol without a value.
QExpansionCoefficients[qexp] gives <|"Components" -> exponent -> coefficient maps in ascending order, "ComponentCutoffs", "Cutoff"|>; leading coefficients come from these maps.
ScalarModularExpression[name, z] gives the inert scalar ingredient name in the variable z: "Eta" (with q^(1/24)), "E2", "E4", "E6", "Delta", "j" (q^-1 leading) and "K" = 1728/j.
The nodes may occur in modular-form definitions and scalar expressions; they never multiply modular-form objects. Option Coordinate ("q" or "tau").
HypergeometricK[a, b, z] gives the inert generalized hypergeometric function Sum_m Product (a)_m / Product (b)_m K^m / m! of K(z) = 1728/j(z), with exact parameter lists a and b (v1's FK).
A denominator parameter that the series reaches as a nonpositive integer fails with SingularHypergeometric; a terminating series that stops first is accepted.

ScalarQSeries[expr, var, n] gives the q-series of a scalar expression in var, numeric constants and scalar ingredients as one-component QExpansionData, keeping exponents below n (n = 0 is valid; a Laurent series keeps its negative powers).
Each ingredient is computed only to the order it can affect (valuation-aware), exactly. Option Coordinate: with "tau" the variable may occur as Exp[2 Pi I r tau].

ModularDerivativeExpression[k, expr, var] gives q d/dq expr - k E2 expr/12 (in the tau coordinate (2 Pi I)^-1 d/dtau expr - k E2 expr/12) as an expression in var and scalar ingredients, using the Ramanujan identities and the derivative of the hypergeometric function.
ModularDerivativeExpression.Example: QExpansionCoefficients[ScalarQSeries[ModularDerivativeExpression[4, ScalarModularExpression["E4", q], q] + (1/3) ScalarModularExpression["E6", q], q, 6]]["Components"]

Details: EvaluateScalarModular[expr, var, point] evaluates a scalar modular expression at TauPoint[tau] or QPoint[q, sheet] by an adaptive q-series and returns <|"Value", "WorkingPrecision", "EstimatedError", "Method", "Order", "Branch", ...|>.
EstimatedError is the agreement of successive orders, not a tail bound. Options as ModularFormEvaluate plus Coordinate.
TauPoint[tau] is a point of the upper half plane, Im tau > 0; fractional powers of q are evaluated as Exp[2 Pi I tau r] on the cusp branch.

QPoint[q, sheet] is the point with q = Exp[2 Pi I tau] and log q = Log[q] + 2 Pi I sheet (sheet 0 by default), for 0 < |q| < 1; equal q on different sheets are different points. QPoint[0] is the cusp, accepted only when the leading terms determine the limit.
Option of ModularFormDefinition and the scalar recipe functions: the independent coordinate.
"q" (default) or "tau". Other values fail with InvalidOption.
Coordinate.Example: QExpansionCoefficients[ScalarQSeries[Exp[2 Pi I tau] ScalarModularExpression["E4", tau, Coordinate -> "tau"], tau, 3, Coordinate -> "tau"]]["Components"]

Details: Option of ModularFormDefinition: the coefficient symbols of the definition, captured held and lowered to FormParameter atoms of the definition's family.

{} (default) or a duplicate-free list of symbols or indexed atoms, distinct from the variable. Patterns and package atoms fail with InvalidOption; values assigned to the symbols never enter the definition.
NormalizationParameters.Example: Lookup[First[ModularFormDefinition[{a q + b q^2}, q, NormalizationParameters -> {a, b}]]["Parameters"], "Label"]

Details: Option of ModularFormDefinition: the family whose relative-normalization unknowns the definition shares (parameter IDs are FamilyID <> ":" <> label).
Automatic (default: a new family) or a string. Other values fail with InvalidOption.
Option of the constructors, coefficient solvers and evaluators: the q-series order used.

Automatic (default: chosen from the accuracy goal and the point, or 6 orders for construction checks) or a positive integer; an explicit order is required to evaluate a finite jet (the result then has EstimatedError Missing["NoTailBound"] or the next-order difference).
Option of the modular-form evaluators: the largest order an adaptive evaluation may use.
2000 (default) or a positive integer; reaching it fails with ConvergenceFailure and the best estimate.
MaxSeriesOrder.Example: FailureQ[EvaluateScalarModular[ScalarModularExpression["E4", q], q, TauPoint[1/2 + (1/100) I], WorkingPrecision -> 20, MaxSeriesOrder -> 30]]

Details: Option of the expensive modular-form computations (coefficient solving, evaluation): a time bound in seconds.
600 (default), a positive number or Infinity; exceeding it fails with TimeLimit and changes nothing.
